newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows Daewoo to raise car stake.
newsitem.headline: India allows Daewoo to raise car stake.

text.p: India's Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has allowed South Korea's Daewoo Corp to increase its stake in car maker DCM Daewoo Ltd to 87 percent, a DCM Daewoo spokesman said on Tuesday.

DCM, which was allowed to raise its stake to 75 percent in the venture late last year, has been allowed to buy a further 12-percent stake following a FIPB decision last week, the spokesman told Reuters.
Until December, Daewoo had held a 51 percent stake and the DCM group had held 34 percent.
Daewoo will increase its stake through an ongoing rights issue, the DCM Daewoo spokesman said. DCM will renounce its entitlement in favour of Daewoo, the spokesman said.

The transfer of shares under the renunciation of rights entitlement was taking place at 24 rupees per share, while the rights issue of five shares for each share held was taking place at 15 rupees per share, he said.
"DCM (stake) will come down from 34 percent to less than 3 percent. Ten percent remains with financial institutions and the public," the spokesman said.
The rights issue, which started in December, will last until February, the spokesman said.
DCM Daewoo's total paid up equity capital will increase to 5.51 billion rupees from 918.4 million after the issue, he added.
Japan's Toyota Motor Corp, which had held a small minority stake in the joint venture, pulled out two months ago in favour of Daewoo, he added.
Daewoo's Cielo was the first foreign car to hit the Indian roads after India allowed in foreign majors under an economic reforms programme launched in 1991.

DCM Daewoo was earlier known as DCM Toyota, which made light trucks with Japanese collaboration until a rising yen put its viability in doubt. Toyota and DCM then joined hands with Daewoo to transform the ailing truck maker into a car company.
Germany's Volkswagen AG said this week it planned to invest $100 million in an Indian car venture.
Volkswagen joined a long list of car makers which include U.S.-based Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp, as well as France's Peugeot.

The companies have taken on Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp, which has been in India for more than a decade through its joint venture with the Indian government, Maruti Udyog Ltd. Maruti currently controls 70 percent of the Indian market.
